answer: Each claim must set an opal into a trellis grown only from its own verified jobs, rooted in a dune whose shape is set by the last close hash. Three peers shake the trellis: an opal set with borrowed jobs flashes the wrong color and falls, so the claim drops with its 100 POA fee burned. The trellis thins with each reuse, so the Nth claim from one operator pays N x 100 POA and needs a fresh root — 10 clones pay 5,500 POA and need 10 roots, each from a different slice of history. One trellis holds one identity; an opal cannot be reset across clones.
